reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space, U:E→ℝ be C², and alpha,eta be nonnegative reals with 0<alpha<=1 and eta<=1. Assume alpha‖v‖² <= D²U(x)[v,v] <= ‖v‖² for every x,v. Given p and xref with gradient U(p)=0 and ‖gradient U(xref)‖² <= alpha dim_R E, set μ=volume.tilted(-U) and piEta=gaussianSmoothing μ (sqrt eta). Then the squared phase quadratic Kantorovich infimum at parameter 1/alpha between (dirac xref)⊗standardGaussian and piEta⊗standardGaussian is at most ENNReal.ofReal(5 dim_R E/alpha). The theorem assumes p and xref; it does not establish their existence. Eta=0 is permitted. The constant is exactly 5 dim_R E/alpha and has no further eta or U dependence.
objects: Actual tilted Gibbs position law, Gaussian smoothing, product standard Gaussian momentum, and initial Dirac-position law.
domains: Finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space.
quantifiers: All admissible E,U,alpha,eta,p,xref; q fixed at 2.
assumptions: C2 Hessian bounded alpha to one, positive alpha<=1, supplied critical point p, small-gradient reference xref, eta<=1.
conclusion: Squared M_(1/alpha) Kantorovich cost at most 5 dim(E)/alpha.
scopes: Does not construct critical point; permits eta=0; no all-q result.
constant_dependencies: Exact 5 dim(E)/alpha independent of eta except eta<=1.
